title: Benchmarking the Explanatory Quality of Open-Weight Vision-Language Models in Face Recognition
abstract: arXiv:2609.21879v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have recently been proposed as promising tools for face recognition, as they can produce natural language explanations alongside similarity scores. This capability is considered appealing for face comparisons in forensic contexts, which require decisions to be transparent and auditable. However, existing evaluations of VLMs for that use case focus mostly on recognition accuracy, while the validity of generated explanations remains unquantified. In this work, we introduce a benchmarking framework for VLM-based face recognition that treats explanation quality as a core evaluation axis. We propose two criteria that explanations should satisfy: relevance, i.e., reliance on identity-stable facial features; and faithfulness, i.e., alignment with the visible image content without hallucinated features. We jointly develop a methodology enabling the quantification of relevance and faithfulness of evaluated models,

translated_title: 开放权重视觉语言模型在人脸识别中的解释质量基准测试
translated_abstract: 视觉语言模型（VLMs）最近被提出作为人脸识别领域颇具前景的工具，因为它们能够在给出相似度分数的同时生成自然语言解释。这一能力被认为对法医场景中的人脸比对具有吸引力，因为此类场景要求决策透明且可审计。然而，现有针对该用例的VLM评估大多集中于识别准确率，而生成解释的有效性仍未被量化。在本工作中，我们引入了一个基于VLM的人脸识别基准测试框架，将解释质量作为核心评估维度。我们提出了解释应满足的两项标准：相关性，即依赖于身份稳定的面部特征；忠实性，即与可见图像内容一致且不包含幻觉特征。我们还共同开发了一种方法，能够对被评估模型解释的相关性和忠实性进行量化。
tldr: 本文提出了一个将解释质量作为核心评估维度的VLM人脸识别基准测试框架，通过相关性（依赖身份稳定的面部特征）和忠实性（无幻觉、与图像内容一致）两项标准及其量化方法，填补了现有评估只关注识别准确率而忽视解释有效性的空白。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a benchmarking framework for VLM-based face recognition that treats explanation quality as a core evaluation axis, proposing relevance and faithfulness criteria along with a methodology to quantify them, addressing the gap where existing evaluations focus only on recognition accuracy.
